articles.title: From historic golf gold to tennis medal miss: India’s biggest hits & flops at Asian Games
articles.summary: India finished fourth at the 2026 Asian Games with 85 medals, including 21 golds, below its Hangzhou record of 106. Archery, hockey, cricket, boxing and wrestling delivered major successes, while athletics topped the overall medal count with 24.

articles.title: FIR lodged after 3 women journalists allege sexual harassment at Delhi protest
articles.summary: On October 3, three female journalists reported instances of sexual harassment to the Delhi Police during a protest. These cases were referred to the Crime Branch for further inquiry.

articles.title: Delhi hit-and-run: Couple in 70s flung into air after SUV hits them
articles.summary: A couple in their late seventies found themselves in a critical situation when an SUV struck them from behind in Kirti Nagar. The driver, Navleen Kaur, reportedly checked on the injured pair before fleeing the scene.

articles.title: One casualty every 23 minutes: Civilians fatalities mount as Ukraine war intensifies
articles.summary: In the first eight months of 2026, the situation in Ukraine has become increasingly dire, with civilian casualties and injuries rising sharply. Reports indicate that nearly 2,500 civilians have been impacted by missile strikes and aerial attacks, targeting both densely inhabited regions and critical infrastructure.

articles.title: NSW planted bitou bush to stabilise dunes; it now threatens native ecosystems across 46% of coast
articles.summary: Bitou bush was intentionally planted along the New South Wales coast to stabilize sand dunes. This plant has since spread extensively, covering 46% of the coastline and threatening native vegetation.

articles.title: Sydney shopper’s A$4 cup turns out to be worth A$75,640
articles.summary: A shopper discovered a unique Chinese libation cup at a thrift shop in Sydney, Australia. They bought the cup for A$4 despite its significant chip.

articles.title: Trump leaks senator’s number after row over clock-change bill: What’s the dispute
articles.summary: Under the current system, Americans move their clocks one hour forward in March and one hour back in November. Moving the clock forward means sunrise and sunset appear one hour later on the clock.

articles.title: Five Indiana engineering students built a 12-hour wearable that helps visually impaired users detect obstacles beyond a cane or guide dog
articles.summary: Rose-Hulman students have developed a remarkable wearable device tailored for visually impaired individuals. This innovative headgear employs advanced sensors to identify surrounding obstacles, providing users with haptic feedback.

articles.title: Hanuman Ansh BO: Day 58 earns Rs 2.10 crore
articles.summary: ‘Hanuman Ansh’, the Neem Karoli Baba devotional film, continues its strong run in its eighth weekend despite ‘Drishyam 3’. It earned Rs 2.10 crore on day 58 from 1,339 screens, down 6.7%.

articles.title: Vijay Deverakonda mourn veteran filmmaker Singeetham Srinivasa Rao
articles.summary: Singeetham Srinivasa Rao, a veteran filmmaker, has passed away at the age of 94. He was known for his inventive storytelling across multiple Indian film industries.

articles.title: Ranvir Shorey says he lost a big film for being 'too vocal' and 'anti-govt'
articles.summary: Ranvir Shorey has revealed that he was allegedly rejected from a big-banner film after being labelled “anti-govt,” “too vocal” and “potentially controversial.” The actor said a trusted source finally confirmed what he had long suspected and described the experience as disheartening. Shorey, known for his outspoken social media presence and acclaimed performances, received support from several users after sharing the revelation.

articles.title: Chiranjeevi condemns AI-morphed video targeting women, seeks dedicated support cell
articles.summary: Chiranjeevi spoke out against the growing prevalence of artificial intelligence being misused to create disrespectful videos aimed at women. He highlighted the urgent need for action within the film industry and called for legal measures against the offenders.
